name: Karnataka
description: A South Indian state known for its diverse performing arts, cuisine, and heritage sites.
historical_context: Home to dynasties including the Vijayanagara and Hoysala empires.

name: Yakshagana
description: A traditional dance-drama combining music, dance, dialogue, costume, and elaborate makeup, depicting stories from Hindu epics.
historical_context: Believed to have evolved from the 16th century, blending folk theatre and classical elements.

name: Bhoota Kola
description: A ritualistic spirit-worship dance performed to appease local deities and ancestral spirits, common in Tulunadu.
historical_context: Rooted in pre-Vedic animistic traditions of coastal Karnataka.

name: Dollu Kunitha
description: A vigorous drum dance performed by men wearing large drums (dollu), typically during festivals.
historical_context: Associated with the worship of the deity Beeralingeshwara.

name: Mysore Dasara
description: The state festival of Karnataka, celebrating the victory of goddess Chamundeshwari over the demon Mahishasura.
historical_context: Popularized by the Wadiyar dynasty of the Kingdom of Mysore.

name: Mysore Palace
description: The historic royal residence of the Wadiyar dynasty, known for its Indo-Saracenic architecture.
historical_context: The current structure was completed in 1912 after a fire destroyed the earlier wooden palace.

name: Ragi Mudde
description: A staple finger-millet dumpling dish, typically eaten with sambar or curry.
historical_context: A traditional food of rural Karnataka valued for its nutrition and low cost.

name: Hampi
description: A UNESCO World Heritage Site containing the ruins of Vijayanagara, the former capital of the Vijayanagara Empire.
historical_context: Flourished as one of the richest cities in the world during the 14th-16th centuries before its destruction in 1565.

name: Kerala
description: A South Indian state known for its backwaters, classical arts, and spice trade history.
historical_context: Historically a major hub of the spice trade with Arab, Roman, and European traders.

name: Kathakali
description: A classical dance-drama known for elaborate makeup, costumes, and codified gestures depicting mythological stories.
historical_context: Developed in the 17th century, drawing from older temple art forms.

name: Theyyam
description: A ritual dance form of worship in which performers embody deities through elaborate costume and trance.
historical_context: Predates Hindu ritual traditions in the region, rooted in ancestor and spirit worship.

name: Onam
description: Kerala's harvest festival, marked by flower carpets (pookalam), boat races, and the Onasadya feast.
historical_context: Associated with the legend of King Mahabali's annual homecoming.

name: Mohiniyattam
description: A classical solo dance form characterized by graceful, swaying movements, traditionally performed by women.
historical_context: Refined in the courts of Travancore in the 19th century under Swathi Thirunal.

name: Vallam Kali
description: Traditional boat races held on Kerala's rivers and backwaters, featuring long snake boats (chundan vallam) rowed by large crews.
historical_context: Rooted in centuries-old riverine traditions, now most famously held during the Nehru Trophy race.

name: Tamil Nadu
description: A South Indian state with a continuous classical tradition in dance, music, and Dravidian temple architecture.
historical_context: Home to Chola, Pandya, and Pallava dynasties.

name: Bharatanatyam
description: One of India's oldest classical dance forms, characterized by fixed postures, footwork, and expressive gestures (mudras).
historical_context: Traditionally performed in Hindu temples by devadasis before its 20th-century revival.

name: Pongal
description: A four-day harvest festival dedicated to the Sun God, marked by cooking the dish 'Pongal' in clay pots.
historical_context: One of the oldest continuously celebrated harvest festivals in India.

name: Chettinad Cuisine
description: A spice-heavy cuisine from the Chettinad region, known for dishes like Chettinad chicken and freshly ground spice blends.
historical_context: Developed by the Nattukottai Chettiar merchant community, influenced by their trade routes across Asia.

name: Meenakshi Amman Temple
description: A historic Hindu temple in Madurai dedicated to Meenakshi and Sundareswarar, famous for its towering gopurams.
historical_context: The present structure was largely built during the Nayak dynasty in the 16th-17th centuries.

name: Jallikattu
description: A traditional bull-taming sport practiced during Pongal, in which participants attempt to hold onto the hump of a charging bull.
historical_context: Believed to date back over 2,000 years, referenced in ancient Tamil Sangam literature.

name: Andhra Pradesh
description: A South Indian state along the Bay of Bengal, known for classical dance, spicy cuisine, and Buddhist heritage sites.
historical_context: Historically part of the Satavahana, Vijayanagara, and later Nizam-influenced regions.

name: Kuchipudi
description: A classical Indian dance-drama form originating in the village of Kuchipudi, blending dance, drama, and music.
historical_context: Traditionally performed by Brahmin men in temple settings before evolving into a broader classical form in the 20th century.

name: Tirumala Venkateswara Temple
description: One of the world's most-visited religious sites, a Hindu temple dedicated to Lord Venkateswara atop the Tirumala hills.
historical_context: Has records of continuous worship and patronage dating back over a thousand years, including major expansions under the Vijayanagara Empire.

name: Telangana
description: A South Indian state carved from Andhra Pradesh in 2014, home to the historic city of Hyderabad and Qutb Shahi heritage.
historical_context: Ruled for centuries by the Qutb Shahi dynasty and later the Nizams of Hyderabad.

name: Bathukamma
description: A floral festival unique to Telangana in which women arrange flowers in concentric layers atop a conical structure.
historical_context: Celebrated over nine days, associated with the worship of the goddess Gauri.

name: Charminar
description: A historic mosque and monument in Hyderabad with four grand arches, an iconic symbol of the city.
historical_context: Built in 1591 by Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah to commemorate the end of a plague epidemic.

name: Maharashtra
description: A western Indian state known for its Marathi culture, Ganesh Chaturthi celebrations, and Maratha Empire heritage.
historical_context: Home to the Maratha Empire founded by Chhatrapati Shivaji in the 17th century.

name: Ganesh Chaturthi
description: A major Hindu festival celebrating the birth of Lord Ganesha, marked by large public idol installations and immersion processions.
historical_context: Transformed into a public community festival by Bal Gangadhar Tilak in 1893 to unite people against British rule.

name: Lavani
description: A traditional folk dance and song form of Maharashtra, known for its powerful rhythm and expressive movements.
historical_context: Historically performed to entertain and boost the morale of tired soldiers, dating back to the 18th century.

name: Ajanta Caves
description: A UNESCO World Heritage Site of rock-cut Buddhist cave monuments featuring ancient paintings and sculptures.
historical_context: Constructed in two phases, roughly the 2nd century BCE and 5th century CE.

name: West Bengal
description: An eastern Indian state renowned for its literature, art, and the grand celebration of Durga Puja.
historical_context: A major center of the Bengal Renaissance in the 19th and early 20th centuries.

name: Durga Puja
description: The largest festival in West Bengal, celebrating the goddess Durga's victory over the demon Mahishasura with elaborate pandals and idols.
historical_context: Recognized by UNESCO as Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2021.

name: Chhau Dance
description: A semi-classical Indian dance form combining martial arts, athletics, and folk traditions, often performed with masks.
historical_context: Practiced across West Bengal, Jharkhand, and Odisha; inscribed on UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list in 2010.

name: Rasgulla
description: A spongy, syrupy dessert made from ball-shaped dumplings of chhena and semolina, cooked in light sugar syrup.
historical_context: Subject of a long-standing Geographical Indication dispute between West Bengal and Odisha over its origin.

name: Rajasthan
description: India's largest state by area, known for its desert landscape, Rajput forts, and vibrant folk traditions.
historical_context: Historically divided among numerous Rajput kingdoms before unifying into a single state after independence.

name: Ghoomar
description: A traditional folk dance performed by women in swirling skirts (ghagra), often at festivals and weddings.
historical_context: Originated with the Bhil tribe and was later adopted widely across Rajasthani royal and folk culture.

name: Pushkar Camel Fair
description: An annual multi-day livestock fair and cultural festival, famous for camel trading, folk performances, and religious bathing rituals.
historical_context: Held for centuries around the sacred Pushkar Lake, coinciding with the Kartik Purnima full moon.

name: Dal Baati Churma
description: A traditional Rajasthani dish of baked wheat rolls (baati) served with lentil curry (dal) and a sweet crumbled wheat dish (churma).
historical_context: Originated as a practical dish for desert regions, as baati could be baked in advance and stored for long journeys.

name: Punjab
description: A northern Indian state known for its agriculture, Sikh heritage, and energetic folk traditions.
historical_context: Historically the seat of the Sikh Empire under Maharaja Ranjit Singh in the early 19th century.

name: Bhangra
description: An energetic folk dance and music form from Punjab, traditionally performed during the harvest festival of Baisakhi.
historical_context: Rooted in Punjabi agrarian traditions, later popularized globally through diaspora communities and fusion music.

name: Golden Temple
description: The holiest Gurdwara of Sikhism, located in Amritsar and famous for its gold-plated structure and surrounding sacred pool.
historical_context: Foundation laid in the late 16th century by Guru Arjan, the fifth Sikh Guru.

name: Baisakhi
description: A harvest festival marking the Punjabi New Year, also commemorating the founding of the Khalsa in Sikh tradition.
historical_context: The Khalsa was formally established by Guru Gobind Singh on Baisakhi in 1699.

name: Gujarat
description: A western Indian state known for its trading history, vibrant textiles, and the Garba/Navratri festival tradition.
historical_context: Home to ancient Indus Valley Civilization sites such as Lothal and Dholavira.

name: Garba
description: A traditional circular folk dance performed during Navratri, often accompanied by dandiya sticks in a related form called Dandiya Raas.
historical_context: Traditionally performed around a clay lamp (garbo) symbolizing life, in devotion to the goddess Durga.

name: Rann Utsav
description: A multi-month cultural festival held on the white salt desert of the Rann of Kutch, featuring folk music, crafts, and tented accommodation.
historical_context: Developed in the 2000s as a tourism initiative to showcase Kutchi culture and handicrafts.

name: Dhokla
description: A steamed, spongy savory cake made from fermented rice and split chickpea batter, a staple Gujarati snack.
historical_context: One of Gujarat's most widely recognized dishes, with regional variants found across the state.

name: Odisha
description: An eastern Indian state known for the Jagannath Temple, Odissi dance, and ancient temple architecture.
historical_context: Historically the center of the Kalinga kingdom, notably the site of the Kalinga War fought by Emperor Ashoka.

name: Odissi
description: One of the oldest surviving classical Indian dance forms, characterized by fluid, sculpturesque body movements.
historical_context: Traces its origins to temple dance traditions depicted in the Odisha's ancient sculptures.

name: Rath Yatra
description: The annual chariot festival of Lord Jagannath, in which massive wooden chariots are pulled through the streets of Puri.
historical_context: One of the oldest recorded chariot festivals in the world, referenced in texts for centuries.

name: Konark Sun Temple
description: A UNESCO World Heritage Site shaped like a colossal chariot dedicated to the Sun God, known for its intricate stone carvings.
historical_context: Built in the 13th century under King Narasimhadeva I of the Eastern Ganga dynasty.

name: Assam
description: A northeastern Indian state known for its tea gardens, one-horned rhinoceros, and the Bihu festival.
historical_context: Historically ruled by the Ahom dynasty for nearly 600 years until British annexation in 1826.

name: Bihu
description: The most important festival of Assam, marking the Assamese New Year with traditional Bihu dance and feasting.
historical_context: Celebrated three times a year, with Rongali Bihu in April being the most widely observed.

name: Kaziranga National Park
description: A UNESCO World Heritage Site and national park famous for hosting the majority of the world's one-horned rhinoceroses.
historical_context: Established as a forest reserve in 1905 following conservation efforts led by Mary Curzon.

name: Nagaland
description: A northeastern Indian state home to numerous Naga tribes, each with distinct traditions, dress, and festivals.
historical_context: Became India's 16th state in 1963, following a long period of British colonial administration.

name: Hornbill Festival
description: An annual festival showcasing the traditions of Nagaland's tribes through dance, music, crafts, and indigenous games.
historical_context: Instituted by the Nagaland government in 2000 to promote inter-tribal interaction and cultural preservation.

name: Ladakh
description: A high-altitude Himalayan union territory known for Buddhist monasteries and distinct Tibetan-influenced culture.
historical_context: Historically an independent kingdom along the trans-Himalayan trade routes before merging with India.

name: Cham Dance
description: A ritual masked dance performed by Buddhist monks, depicting the triumph of good over evil through symbolic movements.
historical_context: Rooted in Tibetan Vajrayana Buddhist monastic traditions practiced across the Himalayan region.

name: Hemis Monastery
description: The largest and wealthiest monastery in Ladakh, famous for its annual Hemis Festival featuring Cham dance.
historical_context: Re-established in 1672 under King Sengge Namgyal, belonging to the Drukpa lineage of Tibetan Buddhism.

name: Uttar Pradesh
description: India's most populous state, home to the Taj Mahal and the classical Kathak dance tradition.
historical_context: Historically part of the Mughal Empire's core territory, with Agra and Lucknow as major cultural centers.

name: Kathak
description: A classical dance form known for intricate footwork, spins, and storytelling, historically performed in Mughal courts.
historical_context: Evolved from temple storytelling traditions and was later refined under Mughal and Nawabi patronage in Lucknow.

name: Taj Mahal
description: An ivory-white marble mausoleum on the banks of the Yamuna, considered a masterpiece of Mughal architecture.
historical_context: Commissioned in 1632 by Mughal emperor Shah Jahan in memory of his wife Mumtaz Mahal.

name: Kumbh Mela
description: The world's largest peaceful religious gathering, held at four river-bank sites in rotation, drawing millions of pilgrims.
historical_context: Recognized by UNESCO as Intangible Cultural Heritage in 2017; rooted in ancient Hindu mythology of the nectar of immortality.
